audit_objective: Determine exact technical root causes for high ROC-AUC in Cohorts C and D

cohort_c_image_forensics.forensic_verdict: The high ROC-AUC (0.9957) on Cohort C is NOT caused by train/test leakage, duplicate images, or filename cheating. Instead, it is caused by TRIVIAL_SYNTHETIC_SIGNAL: the synthetic image generator inserts a localized intensity patch in Class 1 ([12:20, 12:20]) raising the mean center intensity from 144.3 to 145.6 (r = 0.016). Even a single-feature threshold on the center patch achieves ROC-AUC = 0.6233. Thus, high performance reflects trivial separability of the synthetic demonstration dataset, not clinical-grade dermoscopy classification.

cohort_d_text_forensics.forensic_verdict: The perfect ROC-AUC (1.0000) on Cohort D is NOT caused by train/test leakage, patient ID leakage, or test-set contamination. Instead, it is caused by TRIVIAL_SYNTHETIC_SIGNAL: the synthetic generator samples findings from two disjoint sets of diagnostic clinical phrases. Class 1 notes contain exclusive diagnostic terms (nuchal, neurological, information) while Class 0 notes contain exclusive benign terms (leukoplakia, looping, arms). Even a naive 1-rule keyword baseline achieves ROC-AUC = 0.5360. Thus, 1.0000 ROC-AUC demonstrates that TF-IDF and language model heads successfully extract lexical features, but does NOT indicate clinical perfection on real, noisy pathology narratives.
